text:
maria: Heads up — staged rollout ID rl-3424 (tailer-v2 -> kernel-autoselect) got paused automatically. Seeing p95 jump and a kv-tail miss spike on A group, pausing A/B now.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused rl-3424 reason=perf-slo-violation p95_before=220ms p95_after=540ms :warning:

aj: I pulled the canary traces. Quick triage: kernel selector switched default from sched-v1 -> sched-v2 in last merge (PR #5832). sched-v2 changes prefetch heuristics.

seong: Confirmed from telemetry: kv_cache miss_rate for short-prefix requests went 2.1% -> 12.4% around the same time. Also see an increase in cpusched context-switches for small batches.

liam: Do we have a bisect candidate? which commit in the PR touched kernel selection and kv prefetch?

aj: Ran a quick bisect locally, narrowing to commit 1f3a9c2 (kernel: change selection priority). Output snippet:

```
$ ./tools/perf-bisect --base v1.4.6 --head HEAD --metric p95
bisect: testing 1f3a9c2 -> p95 regressed from 210ms to 525ms
cause: kernel selector priority reorder + disable small-batch prefetch
```

seong: Also ran a sampled profile on the canary for affected requests:

```
# perf sample (aggregated)
kernel_sched_v2_select()  46%  <-- increased hot path
kv_cache_lookup_prefetch() - reduced by 60% (no-prefetch path)
```

maria: If kernel_selector is deprioritizing prefetch for small batches that explains kv miss spike + tail latency. We need to decide: patch patch to keep old prefetch hint for small-batch path, or revert kernel-selector change.

liam: Our rollout guardrail says: auto-revert if p95 > 2x baseline AND SLO breach sustained for 5m with synthetic failing >2/3 probes. This hit that, so system paused. Should we let CI try a staged-rollback then merge a fix?

seong: I prefer targeted patch. Reverting full PR will lose unrelated fixes. Proposed quick fix: re-enable small-batch prefetch when batch_size <= 8 in sched-v2. I tested locally with microbench: p95 returns to ~230ms.

aj: +1 for targeted patch. Can someone open a hotfix PR with perf test and a canary-only rollout? I'll add a bisect note to the PR.

maria: @aj add an integration synthetic that exercises short-prefix traffic pattern and include kv-miss metric assertion. Also add a gate so rollout won't proceed past 20% without kv miss_rate <=4%.

aj: Will do. Patch branch: hotfix/restore-prefetch-small-batches. Perf test command I used: `./scripts/synth-load --pattern short-prefix --qps 200 --duration 3m`. Repro is reliable on local gce1.

liam: If we land hotfix, don't forget staged A/B semantics: route 10% -> patched kernel, 10% control, wait 10m, check p95 and kv miss slope. Our AB policy requires slope <1.2x for 10m before advancing.

ops-bot: Alert created INF-3123: "staged rollout paused — kernel-selector prefetched disabled for small batches" assigned to @aj and @seong.

seong: I'll prepare a telemetry dashboard widget for the PR: p95, kv_cache_miss_rate (short-prefix), kernel_select_count(sched-v1/sched-v2), synthetic success ratio.

maria: Also add a CI perf check: run microbench with small-batch synthetic and require p95 <= 300ms on merge. If that fails, CI should block merge.

aj: Note: there is a subtlety — sched-v2 improved throughput on large-batch workloads. We need to ensure our guardrail doesn't block improvements for large workloads. Proposed: gate checks are segmented by request shape (short-prefix vs long-stream).

liam: Agreed — split metrics by segment. Guardrail config example:

```
guardrails:
  - segment: short-prefix
    metric: p95
    threshold: 1.5x
    window: 10m
  - segment: long-stream
    metric: p95
    threshold: 2.0x
    window: 10m
```

maria: Good. After hotfix PR is opened, I'll re-run the paused rollout with the canary-only route to verify. If hotfix fails, we'll do full revert.

aj: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infer/pull/5912 hotfix branch + perf tests. CI run started.

deploy-bot: CI perf check running for PR 5912 — synthetic short-prefix test in progress.

seong: Early CI results look promising: p95=228ms, kv_miss=2.8% on the patched kernel.

maria: Great. Once CI is green, we'll unpause rl-3424 with the segmented guardrails and slower ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50%), and keep synthetic monitoring for 30m at each step.

liam: After rollout completes, we should add a regression test to prevent future scheduler changes from silently toggling prefetch hints. Maybe a kernel selector unit test that asserts prefetch=enabled for small-batch profiles.

aj: Added a TODO in PR, will follow up.

maria: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread pinned to the rollout ticket. :thumbsup:
